frequency_question: How often does Congress successfully pass a joint resolution of disapproval to block a submitted 123 agreement?
membership_rule: Includes all formal 123 agreements submitted by the executive branch to Congress requiring a statutory review period where Congress can pass a joint resolution of disapproval.
window: 1954-2026 (72-year historical observation window matching statutory review precedents)

coverage_note: Universal historical sample of major formal 123 agreement submissions; none have successfully resulted in a binding legislative block.
known_gaps: Informal withdrawals or renegotiations prior to formal submission are excluded as they do not trigger the statutory resolution window.
skeleton: Statutory 123 agreement review cycles submitted to Congress since the inception of the Atomic Energy Act framework.
multiplier: 0 out of approximately 30+ formal civil nuclear 123 agreements submitted and brought to review have been successfully blocked by a joint resolution of disapproval passing both chambers and overriding or avoiding a presidential veto.
validity_reason: The statutory framework governing congressional review of 123 agreements under the Atomic Energy Act remains stable across congressional terms.
